chunks: And everything in it that is narrated from Bakr ibn Muhammad Al-Azdi has been transmitted by me from Muhammad ibn Al-Hasan - may Allah be pleased with him - from Muhammad ibn Al-Hasan Al-Saffar, from Al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, and Ahmad ibn Ishaq ibn Sa'd, and Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from Bakr ibn Muhammad Al-Azdi.

key_terms.أَحْمَدُ بْنُ إِسْحَاقَ بْنِ سَعْدٍ: Ahmad ibn Ishaq ibn Sa'd, a scholar in the chain
key_terms.إِبْرَاهِيمُ بْنُ هَاشِمٍ: Ibrahim ibn Hashim, a scholar in the chain
key_terms.الْعَبَّاسُ بْنُ مَعْرُوفٍ: Al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, a scholar in the chain
key_terms.بَكْرُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ الْأَزْدِيُّ: Bakr ibn Muhammad Al-Azdi, a key narrator
key_terms.مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ الْحَسَنِ: Muhammad ibn Al-Hasan, a primary transmitter
key_terms.مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ الْحَسَنِ الصَّفَّارُ: Muhammad ibn Al-Hasan Al-Saffar, a scholar in the chain

ai.seo_question: Who is the narrator chain for Bakr ibn Muhammad Al-Azdi in this hadith?
ai.summary: This passage exemplifies the rigorous methodology of *al-Saduq* in verifying the authenticity of narrations by explicitly tracing the *isnad* back to the reliable scholar Bakr ibn Muhammad Al-Azdi. By listing intermediate transmitters such as Muhammad ibn Al-Hasan and Al-Saffar, the text underscores the scholarly consensus on the reliability of this specific chain, a critical concern in Shia hadith sciences where the integrity of the transmitter directly impacts the legal weight of the narration.
